title: Choose the visual world for the Siaga test checklist
question: The roll assigned Evacuation Route. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Evacuation Route
options.lineage: ISO 7010 safe-condition signage on BNPB evacuation routes
options.thesis: The test run is an evacuation route: each app area is a station you clear in order.
options.viewport: Green route rail with per-area progress and a You-are-here marker, run summary and failing list on top, case cards with expected-value chips and a Protects line.
options.risk: Green means both 'safe route' and 'pass', so pass and the shell colour must stay distinguishable.

raised.raise: Each case's result sits in one fixed cell at the row's right edge: filled when recorded, hollow when untested.
Only controls you can press carry the action colour; status colour never doubles as a button.
The case ID is the handle everywhere: card, failing list and export row.
Rail and case column lock to one shared grid and gutter.
Status never relies on hue alone: every result also carries a drawn icon and a word.

options.label: Triage Tag Board
options.thesis: Every case is a triage tag; its result is the colour strip you tear off.
options.viewport: Dark header with run totals, a grid of tags each listing expected values and what it protects, result strip at the foot.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of an emergency subject, and triage red/yellow/green collide with fail/blocked/pass meanings.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each case is a coupon; running it stamps PASS or FAIL and nothing disappears.
options.viewport: Navy wallet index of areas with counts, coupons with fare-box expected values and a stamped result.
options.case: Stamps make results unmissable; loses on audience identification, airline travel is not this tester's world.
options.risk: Reads as travel nostalgia if the stamps get decorative.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size, raked glass slides.
options.case: Single type size contradicts the bigger-type request; raked panes hurt scanning.
options.kept: Result as a mark in a fixed cell.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.viewport: Single column of cards with bottom bar.
options.case: A phone pattern on a laptop QA tool; no tie to the emergency world.
options.kept: Action colour only on what can be pressed.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Coded colour strips hide the expected values the tester needs.
options.kept: The ID as the primary handle.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.case: Poster logic, not a working checklist.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: State as line form on one rail.
options.case: Hairline states at tiny type fight the bigger-type request.
options.kept: State shown by shape and word, not hue alone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A test navigator: sidebar tree of cases with status diamonds, detail pane on the right.
canonCard.viewport: Xcode-style test navigator beside the selected case's steps and expected result.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any test tool by design.
